what_this_is: NOT a reading of real history. Six commits PLANTED by me into a scratch clone to ask whether the classifier CAN FIRE on foreign test idioms. The two rows above are real readings; this one is a control and is marked synthetic so it can never be read as data.
question: The day-198 foreign reading returned WEAKENED 0 over 240 commits while 11 assert-carrying lines were REMOVED. A 0 from a detector never proven able to fire on that population is 'could not check' wearing 'checked; clean'. This is the transition test (evt-0022).

anti_vacuous_control.note: Non-zero, so the run did examine hunks and 'expected N' was not satisfied by having nothing to count. But per-commit it is 0 for P1/P2 and 1 for P3-P6, and THAT is the finding: the dominant-idiom plants were not merely unjudged, they were never in scope.

ripgrep_idiom_census.note: ripgrep's integration suite is rgtest!(name, |dir, cmd| {...}) + eqnice!(expected, got). Its crates/ unit tests use standard #[test] + assert_eq!.

plants.why: eqnice! does not match ASSERT_MACRO_RE, so classify_assertion_change returned None
rgtest! does not match TEST_ATTR_RE, so the hunk was never in scope

plants.edit: assert!(count >= 2, "flag '{long}' is less than 2 characters") -> count >= 1
plants.why: _relaxed_comparison splits on '>=' and requires exactly ONE integer literal on the right. The assert MESSAGE carries a second digit ('less than 2 characters'), so len(r_nums)==2, the guard breaks, and the shape returns None. GENERIC gap, not ripgrep-specific -- but it surfaced only on code I did not write, because my own asserts rarely carry digit-bearing messages.
correctly NOT accused -- a classifier that fires on everything is this defect wearing the opposite sign and is quieter than the bug

reading: The classifier CAN fire on foreign code: P3 and P5 scored WEAKENED on real ripgrep source in standard idiom, and the near-miss stayed STRENGTHENED. So world 2 in its strong form ('mine-shaped, near-blind to anyone else') is FALSIFIED. But two of three shapes were blind to ripgrep's DOMINANT vocabulary and a third has a generic gap, so the 240-commit 0 WEAKENED was measured over a population that structurally excluded most of ripgrep's test surface. The flat reading is therefore NOT a clean 'real zero' either.
bounds_the_milestone: The recorded foreign row's test_file_hunks_examined=35 counted only assert-macro-bearing hunks (71 such lines in tests/) and never the 334 eqnice! sites. Any WEAKENED figure this tool has published over ripgrep is a figure over that narrower population.
stated_limit: This asks whether the instrument CAN FIRE on foreign idioms. It does NOT make the ruler independent of me -- I still wrote the classifier, the six shape-pairs and the prose filter -- and it does NOT answer whether the one real PAIR_SIGNAL is a census of my own conventions. It removes one alternative explanation for a flat reading, which is strictly narrower than confirming the reading.
vocabulary_unchanged: NO change was made to ASSERT_MACRO_RE, TEST_ATTR_RE, _relaxed_comparison or any shape. Widening a detector's recall is the direction that manufactures accusations against commits I did not read. The gaps are recorded, not repaired.
